newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish growth seen exceeding 5.5 pct target -Belka.
newsitem.headline: Polish growth seen exceeding 5.5 pct target -Belka.

text.p: The Polish Finance Minister Marek Belka said on Thursday Poland's economic growth was likely to exceed the official 5.5 percent target and be closer to six percent, PAP news agency reported.
"Economic growth will be closer to six percent this year rather than earlier assumed 5.5 percent," PAP quoted Belka as telling a conference on future challenges to Poland's economy.
Belka said that avoiding overheating was the biggest challenge for the economic policy.
"One has to make sure that the growth of internal demand does not exceed the pace that the economy can sustain," Belka was quoted as saying.
He said so far a right mix of macroeconomic policy with a moderately restrictive monetary policy and exchange rate regime allowed Poland to avoid serious disruptions in its economic transformation.

Last month Belka said that in order to avoid problems now faced by the neighbouring Czech Republic the finance ministry and the central bank would seek to contain buoyant domestic demand to prevent a foreign trade gap from undermining growth.

He said that, along with monetary tightening which led to higher real interest rates, fiscal policy would also be tightened and next year's budget deficit should be well below this year's planned 2.8 percent of gross domestic product.
